blurb: Wisconsin River access sections from the Northwoods toward Rhinelander, including separate above-dam and below-dam Otter Rapids accesses, Highway 70, County O and Rainbow Dam. Approximate access areas stay labelled, and dam carries and unresolved route questions appear with their sections.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.routeReview: This start includes the Lac Vieux Desert dam portage and a required carry at the West Shore Road culvert. No continuous dotted river path is shown.

notices.title: Two required carries near the start
notices.text: WVIC describes a 100-foot carry at Lac Vieux Desert Dam, followed about 200 yards downstream by a required road carry at the West Shore Road culvert. Use the signed portages and confirm conditions.

sections.routeReview: Finish at the signed take-out above Otter Rapids Dam. The approximate take-out and below-dam launch are separate markers; a dotted course through the dam is not provided.

notices.title: Take out before Otter Rapids Dam
notices.text: This trip ends at the signed right-bank take-out upstream of the dam. Continuing downstream requires the designated 500-foot carry to the separate below-dam launch. Confirm current signs and access; do not paddle through the dam.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin Valley Improvement Company — Otter Rapids portage diagram

takeOutAccess.accessType: Carry-out / portage access area above the dam
takeOutAccess.operator: Wisconsin Public Service — Otter Rapids facility
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Wisconsin Valley Improvement Company — Otter Rapids portage diagram
takeOutAccess.note: The WVIC aerial diagram identifies a take-out distinct from the downstream put-in. Its approximate location was matched to satellite imagery; no exact shoreline pin or portage track is claimed. The DNR facility inventory names Wisconsin Public Service as manager. Check current signs and access conditions.
takeOutAccess.directions: Finish at the signed right-bank take-out before Otter Rapids Dam, on its upstream/east side. Use the operator diagram and current signs to identify the landing before approaching the dam. If continuing downstream, carry along the designated 500-foot portage to the separate below-dam launch; do not paddle through the dam.

sections.notes: Start at the signed carry-in below Otter Rapids Dam and follow the Wisconsin River to the unimproved Highway 70 access. Expect fast water and boulders near the tailwater and changing wood obstacles. The 4.1-mile planning distance remains preliminary; it is not a surveyed route or a calibrated float-time estimate.
sections.routeReview: The dotted overview begins below Otter Rapids Dam and follows the general river course toward Highway 70. Exact landing approaches and passage around boulders or wood are not mapped; use the signed downstream launch.

notices.title: Start below Otter Rapids
notices.text: Use the signed downstream put-in on the right bank, west of Otter Rapids Dam. The upstream take-out is a separate access. The launch marker is approximate; fast tailwater and boulders require attention to current conditions.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin Valley Improvement Company — Centennial Trail Map 2

putInAccess.accessType: Carry-in canoe/kayak access area below the dam
putInAccess.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR public access inventory; WVIC Otter Rapids portage diagram
putInAccess.note: The DNR facility coordinate is beside the dam and is preserved in the research record. This approximate area center was moved downstream using the WVIC aerial portage diagram and satellite imagery. The exact landing is obscured, so this is not a surveyed or water-edge pin. Community pin suggestions remain subject to review.
putInAccess.directions: From the Otter Rapids public access off Highway 70, follow the signed portage approach to the downstream put-in on the right bank, west of the dam. Launch only below the dam; the upstream portage take-out is a different access. The marker shows the carry-in vicinity, so follow current signs to the shoreline.

takeOutAccess.operator: American Legion State Forest (ownership 'Wisconsin DNR' in the WDNR record)
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — public boat access inventory
takeOutAccess.note: The current DNR record lists an active public ramp facility here; WVIC describes the access as unimproved. Satellite imagery shows the shore-side pull-off but does not establish a distinct constructed ramp edge. The original agency coordinate is retained as an Area marker.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the public access pull-off beside Highway 70 at Centennial Trail mile 46. WVIC identifies an unimproved right-bank landing here. The marker identifies the access area; check the bank and designated parking on arrival, and keep vehicles off the highway travel lanes.

sections.routeReview: The Lake Mcdonald inventory record remains unresolved. Do not treat the published trail overview or satellite imagery as confirmation that a potential barrier can be crossed.

notices.title: County O access and trail guide
notices.text: WVIC identifies the County O public landing upstream of the bridges and describes the river widening into flowage near this take-out. Review the operator guide and current conditions. This does not resolve the separate Lake Mcdonald dam-record conflict.

notices.title: Rhinelander Dam portage required
notices.text: WVIC shows a take-out above Rhinelander Dam and a carry along the west side. The shorter mill route is gated after hours; the alternate follows Phillip Street, Maple Street, Davenport Street, Sutliff Avenue and Ash Street to the lower landing. Review the operator diagram and current signs before launching. Do not paddle over the dam.
